# Complete the customer billing-schedule migration

Finish the service-to-customer migration for recurring billing. Creating a customer must create a monthly billing schedule only when that customer has an offering. When an existing customer gains or changes an `offeringId`, replace any previous billing schedule with a customer-level schedule; an already-missing old schedule is not an error. Preserve the authenticated subject and business ID in the scheduler configuration.

Billing jobs receive `businessID` on the scheduler record and `customerId` in `scheduleParameters`. Resolve the customer and its offering, derive the offering billing-cycle time range, call the existing usage-total invoice path with that exact customer and range, and persist a billing record containing the returned invoice ID. Report processing failures through the existing audit channel instead of leaving the queue job with a partially stored billing record.

Route billing scheduler emissions to `scheduler_billing_queue` with the `billingReport` consumer name. All non-billing measurements must continue to use the normal scheduler queue and their dimension consumer. Finally, a usage read for a customer without an offering should return an empty result rather than fail.

Verify with:

    cd /app && npm run build && npm run test:ci -- --runInBand
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the current state.

steps.message:
The migration is complete. `npm run build` and `npm run test:ci -- --runInBand` both pass (43 suites / 70 tests).

## What changed

**`src/customer/customer.service.ts`**
- `create` now only provisions the monthly billing schedule when the new customer actually has an `offeringId`; otherwise it logs and skips.
- Added `createBillingScheduleForCustomer` / `removeBillingScheduleForCustomer` helpers. The schedule is keyed by `schedulerID = customerId` (customer-level), carries `scheduleParameters: { customerId, businessID }`, `rate: monthly`, plus the authenticated `subject` and `businessID`. Removal swallows `NotFoundException` (an already-missing schedule is not an error) and rethrows anything else.
- `update` captures the pre-update `offeringId`; when the customer gains or changes an offering it removes the previous schedule then creates the customer-level one, preserving subject/business ID. Unchanged offerings leave the schedule untouched.
- `remove` now reuses the shared removal helper.

**`src/customer/dto/update-customer.dto.ts` + `customer.controller.ts`** — hidden optional `subject` so the authenticated `sub` reaches the scheduler config on update.

**`src/billing/billing.service.ts`** — the `billingReport` consumer now takes `businessID` from the scheduler record and `customerId` from `scheduleParameters`, resolves the customer plus its offering via `CustomerService.findOne`, derives the range from the offering's billing cycle, calls the existing `InvoicesService.generateInvoiceForUsageTotal` with that customer and range, and persists a `Billing` record with the returned `invoiceId`. The whole body is guarded: failures are reported via `AuditService.publishEvent({ topic: AuditScope.ERROR })` so no partial billing record is written and the job doesn't die. Customers without an offering are logged and skipped. The now-dead `ServicesService` dependency was dropped (module imports updated accordingly).

**`src/scheduler/scheduler.service.ts`** — `emitOne` routes `schedulerType.billing` emissions to `scheduler_billing_queue` under `billingScheduleConsumers.billingReport`; all other measurements still go to `scheduler_queue` with their dimension consumer name.

**`src/usage/usage.service.ts`** — `findUsageForCustomer` returns `[]` (surfacing as `{ data: [], message: 'No Customer usage found' }`) instead of throwing `ConflictException` when the customer has no offering.

One judgement call worth flagging: `CustomerService` is injected into `BillingService` with `@Optional()`. `BillingModule` imports `PrivateAPICustomerModule`, so it always resolves in the running app — the marker only keeps the processor constructible in reduced DI contexts. Say the word if you'd rather it be a hard dependency.
